key_points.point: The document argues that the path to human-level Text-to-SQL performance lies in scaling inference-time compute and improving model reasoning rather than building complex, multi-stage agentic pipelines. By using RLVR on verified data, the authors demonstrate that models can autonomously discover effective reasoning paths, effectively transitioning from experimental assistants to reliable, autonomous systems. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of achieving transformative capabilities through streamlined, scalable architectures that maximize the utility of underlying model intelligence. The authors note that while inference-time scaling is powerful, it is only effective when the underlying model possesses high intrinsic SQL reasoning capabilities.
key_points.verbatim: Closing this gap represents a critical milestone in Text-to-SQL development, elevating LLMs from capable assistants to reliable, autonomous systems.

key_points.point: The authors advocate for the creation and use of high-quality, expert-verified datasets to unlock the full potential of reinforcement learning for reasoning. By constructing BIRD-Verified, they demonstrate that improving data quality alone significantly boosts model performance, suggesting that the bottleneck to AGI-level reasoning is often the quality of the training data rather than the model architecture itself. This supports the accelerationist desire to centralize and curate human knowledge infrastructure to train more capable, general-purpose AI systems. The document acknowledges that this curation process is labor-intensive, requiring multiple rounds of expert verification to resolve annotation errors.
key_points.verbatim: High-quality, verified training data serves as the foundation of ReViSQL.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the necessity of a rigorous, expert-led verification pipeline to identify and correct pervasive annotation errors in training data. By employing independent SQL experts to perform multi-turn verification and conflict resolution, the authors ensure that the training signal is accurate and reliable, preventing the model from learning spurious patterns. This reflects a safetyist commitment to effective challenge culture and peer review, ensuring that the foundations of AI development are built on verified, high-integrity data. The authors note that automated LLM reviewers, while precise, have low recall, necessitating human-in-the-loop oversight to ensure comprehensive error detection.
key_points.verbatim: We designed and implemented a rigorous data correction pipeline involving independent SQL experts for correction, verification, and conflict resolution.

key_points.point: The authors identify that existing Text-to-SQL datasets contain pervasive annotation errors, which generate spurious reward signals that destabilize the learning process in reinforcement learning. This empirical observation supports the safetyist belief that current alignment and training methods are structurally insufficient if the underlying data is noisy or unreliable. By correcting these errors, the authors demonstrate that the model's reasoning capabilities are significantly improved, highlighting the critical importance of data integrity in ensuring reliable model behavior. The document acknowledges that even with verified data, real-world ambiguity and distribution shifts remain, necessitating robust inference-time reconciliation mechanisms.
key_points.verbatim: When models attempt to learn from noisy data, these pervasive errors generate spurious reward signals, severely destabilizing the learning process.

key_points.point: The document provides extensive evidence that current Text-to-SQL benchmarks are compromised by pervasive annotation errors, including incorrect gold SQL queries, ambiguous questions, and conflicting external knowledge. This degradation of data quality undermines the epistemological integrity of the field, as models trained on such data learn to replicate human errors rather than genuine reasoning. This aligns with the skeptic perspective that AI systems often encode and amplify existing systemic biases and inaccuracies present in their training sets. The authors note that these errors are present in over 50% of instances, representing a fundamental barrier to reliable AI deployment.
key_points.verbatim: Pervasive annotation errors hinder the rigorous evaluation and training of Text-to-SQL models.

key_points.point: The authors argue for the necessity of curating training data for verifiability, moving away from the reliance on massive, unverified synthetic datasets. By demonstrating that rigorous curation is more important than massive creation, they advocate for a more disciplined, data-centric approach to AI development that prioritizes quality and reliability over scale. This reflects the skeptic intention to demystify AI as a standard, fallible enterprise technology that requires careful, manual oversight rather than blind scaling. The document acknowledges that this approach is labor-intensive but essential for achieving reliable, human-level performance in high-stakes applications.
key_points.verbatim: Our research suggests that rigorous curation is more important than massive creation.
